compliance.title: For Schools: Safety & Compliance
compliance.kidIntro: Hi teachers and grown-ups! SpArki is built to be safe, simple, and respectful of kids’ privacy.
compliance.quickFact2: Kid progress can stay on-device, and school progress can be anonymous.
compliance.quickFact3: Teachers can use class codes instead of student names.
compliance.quickFact4: We aim to follow COPPA, FERPA, and CIPA best practices.
compliance.coppaBody: We design SpArki to avoid collecting children’s personal information. For school pilots, we recommend using anonymous student codes (for example: Explorer-42) rather than names or emails.
compliance.ferpaBody: For school use, we treat progress data as an education record. We recommend schools avoid entering student names. Teachers can export class progress as CSV for their own records.
compliance.cipaBody: SpArki teaches safe and kind online behavior and supports school-safe use. Schools should still apply their own filtering and device policies.
compliance.dataPrivacy2: No third-party analytics in the kid experience.
compliance.dataPrivacy3: Progress can be stored locally or synced anonymously for schools.
compliance.pwaBody: On iPad Safari: tap Share, then Add to Home Screen. The installed app can work offline after the first load.
compliance.teacherDashboardBody: Teachers can create classes, assign courses, and view anonymous progress with export tools.
compliance.contactBody: If you’d like to run a school pilot, contact us via the Contact page.
compliance.contactNote: Tip: include your school name, grade level, and device type (iPad / Chromebook).
compliance.legalBody: This page is provided for informational purposes and does not constitute legal advice. Schools should consult their own policies and counsel to determine appropriate use.

aiToolkit.title: AI Implementation Toolkit (CDE-aligned)
aiToolkit.subtitle: Use these teaching steps to keep AI human-first, safe, fair, and transparent.

humanCentered.title: Human-centered AI
humanCentered.body: AI should enhance teaching, not replace it. Keep the educator in charge—model how you check AI ideas, and guide students to make final decisions.
humanCentered.listenText: Human-centered AI. AI should enhance teaching, not replace it. Keep the educator in charge—model how you check AI ideas, and guide students to make final decisions.

studentWellBeing.title: Student well-being
studentWellBeing.body: Use AI in ways that protect emotional safety. Remind students to pause, ask for help, and never share personal details with AI tools.
studentWellBeing.listenText: Student well-being. Use AI in ways that protect emotional safety. Remind students to pause, ask for help, and never share personal details with AI tools.

equityBias.title: Equity and bias
equityBias.body: Discuss that AI can be uneven. Compare answers, ask who might be left out, and treat AI outputs as starting points—not truth.
equityBias.listenText: Equity and bias. Discuss that AI can be uneven. Compare answers, ask who might be left out, and treat AI outputs as starting points, not truth.

transparency.title: Transparency and disclosure
transparency.body: Show students what AI is doing (helping, not deciding). Teach them to explain when they used AI and to double-check results.
transparency.listenText: Transparency and disclosure. Show students what AI is doing—helping, not deciding. Teach them to explain when they used AI and to double-check results.

governanceProcurement.title: Governance and procurement
governanceProcurement.body: Before using an AI tool, teachers and leaders review privacy, safety, accuracy, and what data it collects. Choose tools with clear controls and educator oversight.
governanceProcurement.listenText: Governance and procurement. Before using an AI tool, teachers and leaders review privacy, safety, accuracy, and what data it collects. Choose tools with clear controls and educator oversight.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.coppaBody: SpArki's Adventures Academy is designed for families and is committed to complying with the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA). We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13 without verifiable parental consent.
privacy.noCollectTitle: Information We Do Not Collect from Children
privacy.noCollectBody: In the child-facing experience, we do not collect names, email addresses, photos, voice recordings, or any personally identifiable information (PII) from children. Children access content through a parent-managed session (e.g., a temporary link or this device after a parent has signed in). There is no child account or child login.
privacy.parentOnlyBody: Grown-ups sign in to access the Parent view, unlock the Safety Pass, and (when available) upload homework. Parent consent is required before any upload or processing of content that could contain a child's information. We recommend verifiable consent methods (e.g., as described in our parent materials) where applicable.
privacy.dataMinBody: When homework or similar content is processed, we use it only to generate a learning adventure. We do not store uploaded images or documents after processing. Only anonymized results (e.g., "math addition problem") may be kept in a session. We do not use child data for behavioral advertising or profiling.
privacy.progressBody: Progress (e.g., quiz scores, sparkles) may be stored locally on the device for the child's experience. We do not use cookies or tracking for child-directed sessions in a way that would support behavioral targeting.
privacy.schoolPilotsBody: When a school runs a pilot, teachers may sign in with an account; students may join with a class code using a minimal identifier (e.g., anonymous session or first-name code, depending on setup). Progress for school pilots may be stored with our database provider so teachers can view aggregated results. Optional features (e.g., homework image upload, read-aloud, or generated video) may send content or text to AI or voice providers only as described in your pilot agreement and this policy. Schools may request a subprocessor list and pilot terms before starting.
privacy.ageBandBody: For families, the app stores your selected age band (Sparki Tots, Kids, or Crew) in the browser to tailor lessons and saved progress per band. For schools, teachers may set an age band per class so generated weekly content matches that group. This is not used for advertising.
privacy.rightsBody: Parents can review, request deletion of, or revoke access to any data associated with their use of the service. For questions about this policy or to exercise your rights, please use our Contact page.
